summary.headline: IndoStar Q1 FY27: disbursements up 44% YoY to INR1,235 crore and PAT of INR11 crore, versus a loss of INR424 crore in Q4 FY26.
summary.overview: Disbursements rose 44% YoY to INR1,235 crore, though slightly lower QoQ, with disbursement yield at 17.6%. PPOP was flat at INR92.9 crore and credit cost fell sharply to INR81.4 crore from INR517.3 crore in Q4, which drove PAT of INR11 crore. Management attributes the improvement to the post-January 2025 underwriting tightening, with the old book (about 80% of NPAs) running off over the next 2-3 quarters. Collection efficiency dipped to around 95% and the company held a INR529 crore average excess liquidity buffer that added about INR8 crore of negative carry.

segments.name: Vehicle finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR1,185 crore (+43% YoY from INR831 crore), yield 17.4%; AUM INR7,724 crore. Mix: cars 21% of AUM (from 17%), M&HCV 35% (from 42%), small LCV 21% (from 25%), construction equipment 10% (from 8%), farm 6%.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR50 crore (+85% YoY vs INR27 crore), yield 21.4%, AUM INR217 crore (+24% QoQ). 90+ DPD 0.17%, 125 co-located branches (from 108); average ticket size about INR8.2 lakh.

segments.name: Security receipts
segments.commentary: Net carrying value fell to INR578 crore from INR589 crore after about INR11 crore collections; provision unchanged, coverage up to 64% from 63%.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 disbursement growth of 35%+ YoY expected, based on July trend; management said it should meet or exceed the 35% CAGR target.
FY29 targets unchanged: 35% disbursement CAGR and PAT of INR450-500 crore.

Disbursement yield to hold around 17-17.25% QoQ; cost of borrowing on the book to fall as a 12%+ tranche (about INR250 crore at ~13%) matures in Q2 FY27; overall cost to converge toward ~9% by March 2027.
New book share of AUM to rise to about 85% by Q4 FY27 (68% in June 2026, 60% in March 2026); GNPA and credit cost expected to improve meaningfully over next 2-3 quarters.
Micro LAP AUM to double during FY27; launch in UP and Bihar in August and September; target Micro LAP at 15-20% of AUM over 3-5 years.
Branch network to cross 500 this year (468 now); field sales headcount to rise about 50% by March 2027 over March 2026.
Management overlay of INR49 crore on vehicle finance (West Asia) retained; release depends on portfolio performance and macro.
capex_capacity: Branches: 14 added in quarter to 468 across 24 states and UTs; target to cross 500 in FY27.
Micro LAP operates from 125 co-located branches (from 108) in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Gujarat, with no incremental branch capex; new states UP and Bihar in Aug/Sep.
Field sales force up about 30% in the last six months; target about 50% higher by March 2027 vs March 2026.
Vehicle finance login-to-disbursement TAT down 44% over the last year.
demand_pricing: Management says tighter underwriting since January 2025 (refinements in January and April 2026) has not slowed growth, which is near 40% YoY.
Competition: management says intensity is low in Tier 3-6 and semi-urban/rural areas; origination at about 20% yield, LTV below 40%, with 95%+ of cases self-occupied residential property.
ICRA expects CV wholesale volumes to grow 4-6% in FY27; M&HCV purchases muted in the last 1-2 quarters on price and fuel concerns, while passenger car disbursements now exceed M&HCV.
Micro LAP average ticket size rose from INR5.9 lakh to about INR8.2 lakh over the last year, with management targeting about INR10 lakh over time.
Early delinquency ratio 2.29% (from 5.55% YoY); non-starter ratio 1.65% (from 3.76% YoY); both up marginally QoQ on seasonality.
New-to-credit share down to 4% from 13% in FY24; customers with CIBIL above 725 at 84% (from 63% in FY24).

qa_highlights.question: What is the target mix between Micro LAP and vehicle finance over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets Micro LAP at 15-20% of AUM over 3-5 years, subject to refinement; expansion into more states is planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did collection efficiency dip, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 and Q2 are seasonally softer across the market and that improvement is driven by old-book run-off; about 80% of NPAs are from the old book, and collections are improving month on month over the last 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did yield on loans fall about 40 bps while NIM rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayesh Jain said the 16.5% loan yield was a denominator effect from about INR600 crore of excess liquidity; disbursement yield is about 17.4-17.6%, expected to hold at about 17-17.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did vehicle finance AUM grow only 3% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the tightening from January 2025 that cut disbursements, plus earlier direct assignments and asset sales; AUM growth is expected to pick up as disbursements rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is Micro LAP ticket size growth sustainable and is competition rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Ticket size is 8.2-8.5 lakh, targeted to stabilise around INR10 lakh; management sees low competition in its semi-urban and rural geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for borrowing cost and slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: A high-cost tranche of about INR250 crore at around 13% falls due in Q2 FY27; cost of borrowing is expected to converge toward 9% by March. Slippages are expected to fall as old-book contribution drops from 60% to about 80-85% of the book.

risks_watch: Collection efficiency dipped to around 95% in Q1 FY27; management attributes it to seasonally softer Q1/Q2 and monitors whether it reverts as old-book NPAs run off.
Credit cost and GNPA improvement depends on old-book run-off over 2-3 quarters (about 80% of NPAs from pre-January 2025 book; new book share 68% in June 2026 targeted at about 85% by Q4 FY27).

Yield and margin: P&L loan yield of 16.5% vs about 16.9% in Q4 FY26, with management pointing to a denominator effect from about INR529-600 crore excess liquidity; watch whether disbursement yield holds at 17-17.25% as cost of funds falls toward ~9% by March 2027.
Negative carry from excess liquidity buffer (about INR8 crore in Q1) and the INR49 crore West Asia management overlay on vehicle finance, whose release depends on portfolio performance and macro.

Micro LAP scaling risk: ticket size rising from INR5.9 lakh to about INR8.2-8.5 lakh, new states UP and Bihar launching Aug/Sep, with management acknowledging some stress pockets in Bihar, Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Rajasthan on new books.

Vehicle finance AUM grew only 3% QoQ; M&HCV share fell to 35% from 42% and M&HCV purchases muted for 1-2 quarters on price and fuel concerns; Q2 FY27 disbursement growth of 35%+ YoY is guided but Q2 is seasonally sluggish.
key_quotes: So I think it's fair to say that we should again have in Q2 a 35% plus kind of disbursement growth.
As of June '26, almost 80% of our NPAs pertain to the old book before Jan 2025 and fresh addition in NPA in June quarter is almost 70% contributed by the old book.
We built a good momentum on PPOP growth and PAT growth will follow in the next 2, 3 quarters.
16.5% is more of a mathematical thing because of adjustments on the loan book and the total assets, right?
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on disbursement growth (44% YoY, July trend guided at 35%+ for Q2) and on the expected credit cost and GNPA turn as the old book runs off. It was more cautious and evasive on collection efficiency drivers and on the yield question, where the CFO's explanation of the 16.5% loan yield was given after a clarification round, and it gave only directional answers on regional stress.

growth.why: Management guides to 35%+ YoY disbursement growth in Q2 FY27 (July trend) and holds the 35% disbursement CAGR target to FY29, with Micro LAP AUM set to double in FY27 and branches to cross 500; however, growth is in disbursements rather than AUM (AUM only +6% YoY), and no capex figures or utilisation were disclosed.
